record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.original_question: Is every infinite sequence of real-representable matroids with no U_{3,6}-minor well-quasi-ordered by the minor relation? Equivalently, must there be indices j > i at least 1 such that M_j contains a minor isomorphic to M_i?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.5. If (M1, M2,...) is an infinite sequence of R-representable matroids with no U3,6-minor, then there exist integers j > i ≥ 1 such that Mj contains a minor isomorphic to Mi.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A matroid is called real-representable if it is isomorphic to the matroid determined by the linear dependencies among a finite multiset of vectors in some finite-dimensional vector space over the real numbers. For a positive integer $r$ and a non-negative integer $n \geq r$, the uniform matroid $U_{r,n}$ is the matroid on an $n$-element ground set whose independent sets are precisely the subsets of size at most $r$. Given matroids $M$ and $N$, $N$ is a minor of $M$ if $N$ can be obtained from $M$ by a (possibly empty) sequence of deletions and contractions. A class $\mathcal{C}$ of matroids is well-quasi-ordered by the minor relation if for every infinite sequence $M_1, M_2, M_3, \dots$ of members of $\mathcal{C}$, there exist indices $j > i \geq 1$ such that $M_j$ contains a minor isomorphic to $M_i$.

Prove or disprove: the class of all real-representable matroids that have no minor isomorphic to $U_{3,6}$ is well-quasi-ordered by the minor relation. Equivalently, decide whether for every infinite sequence $(M_1, M_2, \dots)$ of real-representable matroids with no $U_{3,6}$-minor, there must exist integers $j > i \geq 1$ such that $M_j$ contains a minor isomorphic to $M_i$.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication was found that resolves this conjecture. Known well-quasi-ordering results for matroids cover GF(q)-representable matroids of bounded branch-width and, by Geelen–Gerards–Whittle, binary matroids; the real-representable case with the $U_{3,6}$-minor exclusion does not appear to have been settled. Related survey and structure-theory papers list it among open problems on excluding a uniform matroid.
